subject: Marketplace addendum — tax backstop & invoice flow
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@marketplacenimbus.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marco.li@marketplacenimbus.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace addendum: tax and invoicing questions

Hi Aditya / Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft. We reviewed the addendum and have two items that need clarification before Legal can sign off:

1) Tax backstop language: the current draft shifts VAT/GST liability to the reseller in all jurisdictions. We need a carve for taxes imposed on the platform level (we collect and remit in certain markets) — otherwise we expose our partners to unpredictable fees. Can Redwood accept a mutual-tax allocation (Net of taxes collected by the marketplace) or at minimum limit the backstop to direct taxes imposed on the reseller?

2) Invoice flow and timing: marketplace settlements are done on a monthly net-30 basis from our side, while some of your customers require immediate pass-through invoicing. We attached a simple diagram of our invoice flow to explain timing.

Attached: Marketplace_Addendum_v3_redlines.pdf; Invoice_Flow_Diagram.png

Appreciate a quick call if helpful — we have in-house procurement on standby.

Best,
Samantha Price
Head of Partnerships
Nimbus Cloud Marketplace

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@marketplacenimbus.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum: tax and invoicing questions

Thanks Sam — looping in Laura (Legal) and Kim (Sales ops) to scope. Quick notes before Laura takes legal redlines:

- We understand the risk on VAT/GST — Redwood’s intent in the draft was to avoid double taxation on the customer, not to create an exposure for resellers.
- Two asks from us: (a) explicit language that Redwood will provide tax receipts / evidence for any taxes Redwood collects and remits on behalf of customers; (b) a cap/notification requirement if Nimbus expects partner-level tax assessments > $5k per quarter so we can triage with finance.

Laura — any suggested language you want me to propose back to their counsel?

Kim — can you confirm whether Redwood Marketplace deals have historically required immediate pass-through invoices, or whether monthly settlement has been acceptable in most reseller agreements?

Thanks,
Aditya
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@marketplacenimbus.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum: tax and invoicing questions

Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and attachments. I reviewed your redlines (Marketplace_Addendum_v3_redlines.pdf) and attached a short summary with proposed language (Redline_Summary.docx). Topline suggestions:

1) Tax allocation: replace unilateral "backstop" phrasing with a mutual indemnity that distinguishes: (i) taxes imposed on the marketplace operator (platform VAT/GST where Nimbus is the collector) — Redwood will not seek indemnity for these if Nimbus provides evidence of collection/remittance; and (ii) taxes arising from resale activity tied to the reseller’s billing/collecting practices — limited to direct taxes and subject to notice and cure (30 days).

Suggested clause excerpt (for your in-house counsel to review):
"Each Party shall be responsible for Taxes imposed on it by applicable law. In the event a taxing authority assesses Taxes against a Party that are the direct result of the other Party's acts or omissions, the assessed Party shall notify the other Party and provide reasonable assistance to contest or resolve the assessment. Neither Party shall be responsible for Taxes collected and remitted by the other Party on behalf of customers, provided the collecting Party furnishes evidence of payment to the relevant authority."

2) Invoice cadence: propose we mirror Nimbus’ monthly net-30 settlement for pass-throughs but include an option for partners to request accelerated invoices on a per-account basis with 60 days' notice and an associated fee to cover immediate billing ops. That keeps default flow predictable.

3) Operational ask: Kim, we will need a contact at Nimbus finance to validate ACH/Banking info and to test one settlement cycle. Sam — please share the finance POC.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to finalize — I can present the legal compromise to your team.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Marco Li <marco.li@marketplacenimbus.com>

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum: tax and invoicing questions

Laura — thanks for the clear proposal. From Nimbus' perspective this is workable with two concessions:

1) We need a short-form attestation clause in the addendum that Nimbus will be the party to collect and remit platform VAT for identified jurisdictions. That allows our tax team to meet their audit trail.

2) For accelerated invoices, we can accept a per-account opt-in model, but must fix the fee schedule now (suggested 1.5% of accelerated settlement amount or $250 min).

Finance POC: michelle.kwan@marketplacenimbus.com (Director, Marketplace Finance). We can set up a test settlement for May cycle.

I'll accept the redline excerpt with the caveat that our tax attestation language be appended as Exhibit A. We will sign once exhibits are attached and DocuSign link is issued.

—Marco
